sources.title: Valeria Simoncini, Computational Methods for Linear Matrix Equations, SIAM Review 58(3), 2016; author-hosted full-text PDF
sources.locator: Complete 58-page PDF inspected. §3, PDF pp. 6–7, Kronecker product, vec and Lemma 3.1; §4, PDF pp. 7–12, Sylvester vectorization, spectral solvability criterion, sep definition, Schur-based Bartels-Stewart and block substitution; §5.1, PDF pp. 20–21, stable Lyapunov uniqueness and positivity; §5.2.2, PDF pp. 25–28, low-rank ADI recurrence, conjugate shifts and rational error formula (5.8).
sources.support: Independent full-text survey for Sylvester/Lyapunov equation conventions, Kronecker vectorization, the spectral solvability condition, separation, Schur substitution, Hurwitz Lyapunov solutions and low-rank ADI. Literature statements that are quoted without proof are completed locally in their authored items. The local ADI recurrence fixes the exact left-shift convention and proves its residual identity directly.

contents.name: §3, Lemma 3.1: vec(AXB)=(B^T tensor A)vec(X), with the complex transpose convention
contents.support: The carrier defines column stacking and the Kronecker blocks explicitly and proves the two Sylvester summands by component indices; the source identity is not treated as a complete proof.

contents.name: §4, equations (4.1) and (4.3): vectorized Sylvester system and unique solvability iff spec(A) and -spec(B) are disjoint
contents.support: The source gives the Kronecker system and criterion with a cited matrix-analysis result; the carrier proves the criterion using triangular forms and the actual Kronecker block diagonal.

contents.name: §4.1: separation as the minimum Sylvester-map norm on unit matrices and its role in residual conditioning
contents.support: The definition fixes the Frobenius-induced map minimum modulus, matching the source convention. The inverse bound and the residual-to-forward-error estimate are proved locally.

contents.name: §4.2: Schur-based Bartels-Stewart transformation and triangular or real quasi-triangular substitution
contents.support: The local procedure states finite-budget and exact-certificate failure branches, explicit block traversal order, and separated local Sylvester solves; separate items prove conditional exact correctness and the arithmetic count.

contents.name: §5.1: Hurwitz Lyapunov equation, uniqueness, positive-semidefinite solution and observability strictness statement
contents.support: The survey statement is not used as a proof. The carrier establishes decay, integral convergence, the differential identity, uniqueness, and the exact kernel-trajectory strictness condition.

contents.name: §5.2.2: LR-ADI factor recurrence, shift conjugacy for real data, and rational error identity (5.8)
contents.support: The source recurrence uses a right-factor convention; the authored item uses the controlling plan's left-shift residual convention and proves the factor identity by direct expansion. Conditional convergence is proved only from an explicit operator rational bound.

sources.title: Elias Jarlebring, Numerical Methods for Lyapunov Equations, Lecture Notes in Numerical Linear Algebra, 2017
sources.locator: Complete 15-page lecture-note PDF inspected. §4.1, PDF pp. 1–2, vectorization and Theorem 4.1.1 unique solvability (the proof is assigned as an exercise); §4.2, PDF pp. 2–5, real Schur block substitution, Bartels-Stewart algorithm and operation-count discussion; §4.3, PDF pp. 5–6, stable Lyapunov exponential integral.
sources.support: Independent full lecture-note treatment of the real Lyapunov special case and Schur-block substitution. Its uniqueness proof is explicitly left as an exercise, its cubic complexity discussion is not a complete count, and its integral formula is stated without a proof; each corresponding library argument is supplied locally.

contents.name: §4.1, equation (4.2): vec(AXB) identity and vectorized Lyapunov equation
contents.support: The local lemma expands both Sylvester terms entrywise and proves that column vectorization preserves the Frobenius norm.

contents.name: §4.1, Theorem 4.1.1: Lyapunov uniqueness criterion stated with proof assigned as an exercise
contents.support: The source's exercise is not treated as a completed argument; the local theorem proves the general two-matrix criterion over both real and complex fields.

contents.name: §4.2, equations (4.6)–(4.15) and Algorithm 1: real Schur blocks and backward block substitution
contents.support: The real block traversal and small diagonal Sylvester solves inform the finite procedure. The item states pivot-separation and exact-certificate failures; its separate theorem proves correctness.

contents.name: §4.2, Bartels-Stewart complexity paragraph: cubic dense-cost estimate with detailed other-part count assigned as exercise
contents.support: The lecture-note estimate is not used to discharge the proof. The local theorem counts Hessenberg work, linearly many sweeps, transforms and block substitutions.

contents.name: §4.3, equation (4.16): exponential integral for the stable Lyapunov solution
contents.support: The equation convention is translated to AX+XA^*+Q=0; the local proof establishes convergence, identity, uniqueness and positivity.

sources.title: MA1111 Linear Algebra I, Lecture 10: Determinants by Laplace Expansion and Inverses by Adjoint Matrices, Trinity College Dublin, Michaelmas 2016
sources.locator: Complete 5-page lecture-note PDF inspected. §2, PDF pp. 2–3, adjugate definition, the entrywise proof of A adj(A)=det(A)I, and the inverse formula; §1, PDF pp. 1–3, Laplace expansion and the determinant-zero fact for repeated rows.
sources.support: The notes prove the adjugate identity by expanding each product entry: the diagonal entries are Laplace expansions, and each off-diagonal entry is a determinant with a repeated row. The lecture labels indices from 1; the local carrier reindexes these rows and columns to the library supplier’s 0-based convention. It supplies the complete argument over an arbitrary field and derives the inverse and singularity cases from its declared determinant criterion.

contents.name: §2, theorem: A adj(A)=det(A)I and the cofactor inverse formula
contents.support: The item expands the (i,j) product entry with zero-based indices, treats i=j by Laplace expansion and i!=j by replacing a row to obtain repeated rows, then derives the inverse formula over the declared field.

full_text_read.scope: The complete lecture note, especially §1–§2 on Laplace expansion, repeated-row determinants, the adjugate identity and the inverse formula.
